newsitem.title: GERMANY: Santer says jobs pact makes EMU more balanced.
newsitem.headline: Santer says jobs pact makes EMU more balanced.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer on Tuesday said inclusion of an employment chapter in the Maastricht treaty would make monetary union more balanced.
Santer, speaking to German Radio, said the jobs pact, that puts employment at the top of EU priorities without sacrificing a fiscal stability pact, was not just a sweetener for the French.
"Certainly I believe that it is more than that because there is an expansion of the definition of monetary union to include an economic union," he said.
He said the agreement re-establishes a balance between the economic and the social aspects of the European Union.
"It is important to express that the (European) Union is not only a common market, that it is not only monetary policy, but beyond that it has a social dimension," he said.

Both the stability and jobs pacts were agreed on Monday by EU leaders at a summit in Amsterdam. The jobs deal was forged after France's new left-wing government threatened to delay the common currency timetable unless EU agreed to accompany the stability pact with greater emphasis on the social aspects of the monetary union.
